question: Why did container ships get slower?
answer: Deliberately, after 2008. Fuel use rises steeply with speed, so cutting speed by around a tenth saves a disproportionate share of the fuel. When freight rates collapsed and fuel stayed dear, slowing down beat sailing fast — and much of the fleet never sped back up.
move: The world's cargo slowed down on purpose and mostly stayed slow.
source: Slow steaming, adopted across container shipping post-2008
reference: Cariou, Is slow steaming a sustainable means of reducing CO2 emissions from container shipping?, Transportation Research Part D, 2011
